title: Thomas Crapper didn’t invent the flush toilet
body: A flushing toilet was described by Sir John Harington, godson of Elizabeth I, in 1596. A key improvement came in 1775, when Alexander Cumming patented the S-shaped trap: a bend that always holds some water and blocks sewer smells. Victorian plumber Thomas Crapper ran a successful sanitaryware firm and patented improvements such as the floating ballcock, but the idea that he invented the toilet, or that ‘crap’ comes from his name, is a myth.

steps.label: A flush pushes water through the bend
Some water stays in the dip
That plug of water seals the pipe
Sewer smells can’t get past it

slides.question: What does Cumming’s S-shaped trap of 1775 actually do?
options: Holds water that blocks sewer smells
slides.explanation: The bend always holds some water, and that plug of water blocks smells from the sewer. Crapper later patented improvements such as the floating ballcock.

slides.heading: Match the man to his contribution
slides.explanation: Crapper set up as a sanitary engineer in 1861 and held nine patents, but none for the flush toilet itself.
